proposals.default_action: No patient decision; trial-level endpoint (stimulated C-peptide, MMTT AUC).
proposals.reason: Clarification 29: D1 is 1 at most for a research endpoint and no individual patient decision is named. Both scorers (V23, V24) gave 1; V23 noted 0 as an alternative, but counselling about residual function keeps 1. Unchanged. Measure type: C-peptide, post-meal stimulated.

proposals.default_action: Classify from clinical features and antibodies; read C-peptide uncorrected in CKD.
proposals.reason: Interpretation limit (kidney clearance raises C-peptide); no validated eGFR correction and no accepted action depends on an adjusted value, so no individual decision is named (clarification 29). Both scorers (V17, V18) gave 1. Unchanged. Measure type: C-peptide, glucose/C-peptide ratio, UCPCR.

proposals.default_action: Insulin and DKA treatment (same with or without the result).
proposals.reason: Current 2.5 is the mean of V17 (3) and V18 (2). Clarification 28 and D-38: low C-peptide is criterion 3 of 3 in the Japan Diabetes Society fulminant T1D criteria, a national diagnostic criterion elsewhere, so D1 is 3, the same reading as row 47. The US reading (no guideline uses it; treatment unchanged) belongs in D3, D7 and S, not D1. Measure type: C-peptide (urinary or serum, stimulated).

proposals.default_action: Insulin-treated patient of unclear type stays on insulin.
proposals.reason: Current 2.5 is the mean of U4 (2) and U5 (3). Under clarifications 18 and 26 the harm is that of the default without the result: unnecessary insulin (hypoglycaemia, burden) or a missed MODY or non-insulin option, moderate and delayed. DKA arises from a wrong result or a wrong withdrawal, not from absent information, so it is not the marginal harm. Moves rank-relevant S from 0.625 to 0.5 on the 0-1 scale.

proposals.default_action: Pioglitazone given on the other guideline trigger (stroke or TIA with prediabetes) without a HOMA-IR value, or at clinician judgement.
proposals.reason: Current 2.5 is the mean of U4 (2) and U5 (3), and U5 scored recurrent-stroke severity, which clarification 18 forbids. Both scorers noted that clinicians can treat without HOMA-IR, and no source read shows benefit differs by HOMA-IR stratum. Marginal harm is treating a low-IR patient who gains less (oedema, weight, fracture risk) or leaving out a patient who would benefit if the default is not to treat; symptomatic or reversible, 1. If the default were withholding pioglitazone, S would be 2; recorded as the alternative.

proposals.default_action: Continue insulin in an adult of doubtful diabetes type.
proposals.reason: Current 1.5 is the mean of V4 (1) and V5 (2). The default (continue insulin) is not itself dangerous; the marginal harm is unnecessary insulin with injection burden and hypoglycaemia, symptomatic and reversible. Withdrawal-related DKA belongs to a different default and is not scored. Alternative 2 if hypoglycaemia in older patients is weighted as moderate.

proposals.default_action: Continue insulin until evaluated, after DKA in a person with suspected ketosis-prone diabetes.
proposals.reason: Current 1.5 is the mean of V4 (1) and V5 (2). Same default and same harm as row 31: unnecessary lifelong insulin in patients with preserved function, reversible. DKA recurrence (3) applies only if empirical withdrawal were the default; not scored. Consistent with row 31.
